'''Norman N. Li''' ({{zh|c=黎念之|p=Lí Niànzhī}}; born December 25, 1932, in [[Shanghai]]), is a [[Chinese-American]] [[engineer]] and [[scientist]] noted for his inventions and development of liquid membrane technologies.

==Biography==
Li graduated from the National Taiwan University in 1954. Li went to continue his study in the United States, received M.Eng in Chemical Engineering from the [[Wayne State University]] in 1957 and PhD from [[Stevens Institute of Technology]] in 1963.  Dr. Li was also awarded an honorary doctorate from the New Jersey Institute of Technology<ref>http://commencement.njit.edu/2008/docs/PROGRAM_08.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303212159/http://commencement.njit.edu/2008/docs/PROGRAM_08.pdf |date=2016-03-03 }} 'NJIT : NJIT Commencement Ceremony 2008'</ref>

Li worked for [[Parke-Davis]], [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. In 1960, Li was a lecturer at NJIT. In 1963, Li was a Senior Scientist of [[ExxonMobil]]. Li was the director of the separation technology research institute of [[UOP LLC|UOP]], and the director of [[AlliedSignal]] science & technology division. Li was the President of the NL Chemical Technology, Inc. based in [[Illinois]].

==Awards and honors== 
Li has been given numerous awards and prizes or his innovation and leadership in membrane and separation technologies, including,
* 1988, the [[Alpha Chi Sigma]] Award for Chemical Engineering Research,
* 1988, the ACS Award of Separation Science and Technology,
* the Clarence G. Gerhold Award from the American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE),
* 1995, the Ernest W. Thiel Award,
* 2000, the AIC Chemical Engineering Practice Award,
* 2000, the [[Perkin Medal]] from the [[Society of Chemical Industry]],
* 2001, the ''Lifetime Achievement Award'' from the World Congress of Chemical Engineering,
* 2001, the Fujimura Award for Lifetime Achievement in International Technology Cooperation and Development
* 2006, the ''Founders Award'' from the American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://newsletter.sinica.edu.tw/en/news/read_news.php?nid=816 |title=Academician Norman N. Li Awarded Honorary Doctorate by NJIT |access-date=2009-12-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303171323/http://newsletter.sinica.edu.tw/en/news/read_news.php?nid=816 |archive-date=2016-03-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* 2013, the Stevens Honor Award from Stevens Institute of Technology <ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.stevens.edu/sit/stevens-awards-gala/2013-winners |title=Stevens Awards Winners 2013 &#124; Stevens Institute of Technology |access-date=2014-01-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140109151357/http://www.stevens.edu/sit/stevens-awards-gala/2013-winners |archive-date=2014-01-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In May 2008, Li was awarded an [[Honorary degree|honorary doctorate]] by [[New Jersey Institute of Technology]] (NJIT). The ''Dr. Norman N. Li Distinguished Lecture in Chemical Engineering'' at the [[Wayne State University]] College of Engineering is named after him.

Li was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Engineering]] in 1990.<ref>United States National Academy of Engineering Membership Dictionary: [http://www.nae.edu/nae/naepub.nsf/Members+By+UNID/22F3CAA5270F38888625755200622D40?opendocument Dr. Norman N. Li]</ref> Li is also an Academician of the [[Academia Sinica]]. Li was elected Foreign Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1998.
